ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The pattern shown in the diagram is constructed using semicircles. Each semicircle has a diameter that lies on the horizontal axis shown and has one of the black dots at either end. The distance between each pair of adjacent black dots is $1 \mathrm{~cm}$. The area, in $\mathrm{cm}^{2}$, of the pattern that is shaded in grey is $\frac{1}{8} k \pi$. What is the value of $k$ ?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure has a horizontal axis, on which equally spaced black dots are arranged, with the distance between adjacent black dots being 1 cm. The gray region is composed of semicircular band-shaped regions gradually going outward around the center; the diameters of these semicircles all lie on the horizontal axis, and the endpoints are black dots. Looking along the spiral from the center outward, each layer of gray band can be regarded as the difference of the areas of two adjacent semicircles. The outermost corresponding gray boundary semicircle spans 11 unit intervals. Reasoning: Let the area of a semicircle with diameter n cm be A_n, then A_n = (1/2)π(n/2)^2 = (π/8)n^2. The gray spiral is composed of consecutive differences: A_1 - A_0, A_2 - A_1, ..., A_11 - A_10. After adding, telescoping cancels, and the total gray area is A_11 = (π/8)·11^2 = (121/8)π. The area in the problem is written as (1/8)kπ, so k = 121.

method.method_draft: Read the diagram from the center of the spiral outward. The black dots on the horizontal axis are 1 cm apart, and the grey spiral is made from successive semicircular strips whose bounding semicircles have diameters increasing by 1 cm each step, up to the outermost grey-bounding semicircle spanning 11 unit gaps. Let A_n be the area of a semicircle of diameter n, so A_n = (π/8)n^2. The shaded pieces can be treated as successive differences A_1-A_0, A_2-A_1, ..., A_11-A_10. Add these: the sum telescopes to A_11 = (π/8)11^2 = (121/8)π, so k = 121.
